THE HISTORY     A  small  band  of  non - free  flees  from  cruel  rulers  in  an  empty land. On the way there they have to pass the Gray  Mountains and are almost destroyed by a dragon. But their  leader, Brandur, faces the dragon with such willpower and  determination  that  the  dragon   begins  to  fear  for  his  immortal life. He lets the crowd pass and has since sent his  creatures to kill Brandur.   The game "The Legends of Andor" begins about 80 years  later. Brandur became the king of the small people and the  country got the name "Andor" .. .       THE CREATURES     Tarok and the creatures   Krahal, the magical place that gave the dragon power and energy, was deeply shaken  hundreds of years ago. The dragons died and only one of them survived. From the  depths of Krahal crawled creatures, unspeakable creatu res with destructive powers.  At some point, they left Krahal and scrambled in the mountains and forests of Andor  to fight and kill for the last dragon.     They were Gors, evil creatures that dreaded humans and dwarves alike. Her arms and  legs were dotted wit h scales. Her hands were two huge, pointed and sharp horn claws.  Bent  and  submissive  was  her  posture  and  they  seemed  to  be  waiting  without  understanding for the orders of the dragons.     There were other creatures, Skrale and Wardraks. Skrale were very tall  and muscular.  They carried huge swords in their hands. On arms and legs, their bodies were covered  with armor pieces to protect them in combat. They were dangerous, because they  made their own decisions and could win a fight with reason.       Echo - like, tall an d fast were the Wardraks. Her eyes glowed like coals, vicious and mean. They were fast as  arrows and could jump up the sharpest rocks and kill with their sharp claws, which got in their way.     Her  master,  the  dragon who  survived,  was  named  Tarok.  A  huge  cre ature.  Monstrous,  razor - sharp  scales  covered the gigantic body. Giant wings protruded from the plucking and the head sat on a snakelike neck. Blood  red and mean, his eyes stared. There was no one who did not fear Tarok, and for centuries he was in the Gray   

Mountains and made it impossible to cross the mountains. Brandur, however, faced the dragon. His willpower  and determination made the dragon fear for its immortal life. He let Brandur and his friends pass and since  then sent out his creatures to kill him.   Years later, when Tarok attacked the Rietburg, it was only the heroes of  Andor who opposed him.     REKA THE WITCH     One day Sabin found a child at the well. It was very early in the morning and the child  was wrapped in white cloths and slept soundly. Sabin pick ed up the child and brought it  to the Krahdern, which should determine what happened to the child. In the city the  power lay with the Krahdern and Sabin belonged to the Ambacus, the unfree of the  country. Radak, head of Krahd, decided that the child should   stay with Sabin until it was  old enough to serve the Krahdern. So she took the child, a girl and gave her the name  Reka. Reka was a bright and inquisitive child and Sabin had a hard time with her. But  Reka made life easier for Sabin, because Reka always m anaged to give Sabin strength for  everyday life through something. Sometimes she just took her hand and looked at her  and it seemed like she was breathing new powers. Sabin never knew what it was, but she  feared that this gift would be known to the Krahder n.      The older Reka became the better she could use her skills. She helped a lot of Ambacus in distress, but no one  knew exactly what that help was, but anyone who got it could say, "I'm feeling better now." Reka became a  strong young woman trying to escape  at the side decided by Brandur. Her strength helped her escape and many  years later she was indispensable to the heroes of Andor.     THE TROLLS     The trolls have always lived in Andor. They were gigantic and simple creatures  with enormous power. They killed arbi trarily and tortured humans and animals.  Long before Brandur and his friends reached Andor, the keepers of the watchful  forest and the trolls fought inexorably.   Troll's arms and legs were huge muscles, and her upper body seemed to tower over  everything els e. Weapons they did not carry with them, but took in the fight, what  appeared to them big enough, tree trunks or rocks. Smaller objects could not reach  them with their huge paws. They also influenced the fate of Andor. Twenty years  before the game "The Leg ends of Andor" begins the last great battle takes place on  the summer rock. This battle ended the troll wars and since then there are very few  of them.       OUTLOOK     The legends of andor  -   what hap pened next ...     After Tarok defeated the dragon, troubled times en sued, reports of which entered the  archives of the Tree of Songs as "The Legacy of the Dragon."     The creatures were out of whack. They came from afar and ventured to Andor. Soon  the heroes realized that the fear of Tarok had kept many evil creatures away f rom  Andor.  After  the  fall  of  the  dragon,  Varkur,  the  Dark  Magician,  returned.  His  transformation was dramatic and he was more dangerous than ever. His desire for  power became the greatest danger to Andor. But there were also bright spots. With  the disappea rance of the dragon, commerce flourished, the art of cartography and also  the  builders  of  the  country  had  their  hands  full.  Years  passed  before  the  heroes  responded to a call for help from far - off Hadria and began the dangerous voyage to  the north. There t hey experienced another great adventure.             

KEN DORR, MERRIK AND GILDA     Ken Dorr, the thief   Ken Dorr was a descendant of the first Andori, who escaped from Krahd together  with Brandur. In the troll wars, his parents' farm was completely destroyed and  his family   was left with nothing. In order to survive they relied on the charity of  others. For Ken Dorr, this was a serious blow because he was a proud boy and  despised having to live on the alms of others. So he started stealing to take care of  his family. Later,  he was received as a soldier in the service of King Brandur and  proved a skilled swordsman. His preference for stealing, however, he did not put  off.  After  spending  some  time  at  the  castle,  he  was  discovered  stealing  and  banished from the castle. At that t ime, exile from the castle was a death sentence.  Before he left the castle, he still took what he needed to survive. Through his  fighting skills Ken Dorr made it to the coast of Andor. There he smuggled himself  aboard a merchant ship to leave Andor and sta rt a new life. From then on, little is  known about his life, but when the rumor went around, the terror of Andor, the  dragon  Tarok  was  finally  defeated,  he  returned  to  Andor  and  again  caused  mischief.       Merrik, the cartographer   Born in the Woods, Merrik  studied the art of calligraphy and archiving from childhood. He proved to be a  skilled bookbinder and decorated his scrolls with fine drawings. But he was filled with a constant restlessness.  He was not made to write down the adventures and legends of othe rs  -   he wanted to experience them himself.  As a 12 - year - old boy, he was allowed to accompany Melkart the supreme keeper and some other keepers on a  trip to Rietburg and was fascinated by the great defenses. When they were ambushed on the way back, he  barel y survived because he was of a feeble build and barely able to carry a wooden sign. But even if he was not  a fighter or archer, his thirst for adventure was unbroken. Soon he began to draw the path between castle and  forest and tried to learn from written  records more about the geography of the country Andor.     Merrik's drive was unfulfilled and finally, at the age of 16, he was allowed to walk. He visited the Rietburg again,  moved south through the Rietland and explored the Southern Forest. When he returned   to the tree of songs  about a year later, he looked many years older. In his luggage he had the most detailed map you have ever seen.  The value of these maps was hardly high enough to estimate, because many there marked ways or sources  were only the fewest   known.     Merrik spent many years studying Andor's cartography and is said to have even charted the southern foothills  of the Gray Mountains and was the first person in years to ever see the land of the Krahders with his own eyes.  He had often been in dange rous situations during all his walks. And because he himself was not a good fighter,  he soon concluded an agreement with a young wolf warrior named Orfen. This accompanied him frequently  and kept him all sorts of evil creatures from the body. In later year s, Merrik made a name for himself above all  with his nautical charts from the Hadrian Sea.     Gilda, the innkeeper of the tavern   Gilda's  father  was  a  Keeper  of  the  Watchful  Forest.  His  name  was  Kallun  and  he  was  on  an  important  assignment to Rietburg. At the request of King Brandur Kallun should teach him reading an d writing. Although  the king was a clever mind, he had received no education as a slave in Krahd. Gilda's mother was Bertha and  met Kallun in the tavern of Andor. Bertha instantly fell in love with him. When Kallun talked to the other tavern  guests, he was   amazed how many stories and legends the men and women of old days knew and he listened  eagerly. At first he hardly noticed Bertha until she herself recounted a particularly rude and funny ballad about  the "drunken troll". Bertha was spirited and funny and   the ballad ended in loud cheers and applause. A lot of  mead filled the pitchers before the next morning dawned. Kallun promised to return when he left. He never did,  and nine months later Gilda was born. She spent her childhood in the tavern and had inher ited her mother's  serene mind. Gilda had a beautiful voice and guests often came from far away just to hear her sing. In later  years she preferred to listen to the guests rather than to sing, for there was much happening in the land of  Andor, and many lege nds were given to her. In a way, she too, like her father Kallun, had become a Keeper,  though she never wrote down the legends, but always kept them in her head.     Years later, when the heroes of Andor were searching for the Star Shield, there were those wh o believed that it  had been Gilda who had given them the crucial clue to finding the Star Shield.   

THE TAVERN TO THE DRUNKEN TROLL     Not so long ago, the landlady Gilda told of her grandfather's story:   At that time grandfather Erloth had a wooden cart with whi ch he sold mead and  wine  to  the  surrounding  farms.  With  a  particularly  large  load  he  rumbled  towards the market bridge to delight the dwarves with his goods. But on his way  the  unbelievable  happened:  He  was  attacked  by  a  giant  troll!  Fortunately,  grandfath er  was  able  to  escape  unseen  in  the  high  reef  grass.  But  the  troll  destroyed his car and made his way over the barrels. It seemed to taste good, for  when Erloth came back to see if there was anything left to save, he saw a huge  figure stagger away, which w as not surprising, for he had almost drained the  entire supply of mead and wine. This was followed by some amusing incidents  with Andor peasants! Instead of chasing and eating them, the troll lurched past  them singing or sleeping in their stables.       However , the cart was destroyed and so Grandfather decided to build a small stand out of the ruptured parts  and sell the remains of mead and wine from the place of the raid. The stand soon became a small hut. Many  travelers came and told what happened here and th ere in the country. And so, from the remains of the old cart,  the tavern became the drunken troll and I, Gilda, the granddaughter of Erloth, became after my mother, the  landlady.   VARA, THE WATER SPIRIT     Kheela, the guardian of the River Lands and Janis, her  son stood on the bank of  the Narne. Dusk had fallen and it was getting cold. Janis pointed his finger to the  other shore, where the silhouette of a woman was to see and asked: "Mother,  what is she actually?"   Kheela looked up and said, "That's a long story,   and when you're old enough, I'll  tell you."   "Mother, please, I'm eight already." Kheela smiled at her son. "You may be right. I  was seven when my dad spoke about her for the first time. Alright then sit down  and listen carefully.   "Her name is Vara. Many h undred years ago she lived, like all water spirits here in  the river. "     Janis's eyes widened: "Is she that old?"   "Yes, she is very old and has done a lot for the people here."   "There are more who are like her?"   "Yes, but they live in this water. They are t he soul of the river and keep it alive. Vara is not here voluntarily. She  was  banished  by  her  people.  "Kheela  took  a  deep  breath  and  then  continued,"  Your  great - great - great - grandfather was a simple farmer named Etore. He ordered his fields and cared for hi s parents and siblings. But  that was not all, he also cared for those who needed help. He was young and strong and wherever he was in  trouble he came and offered his help.   One day something terrible happened. A big fire had broken out in the village. Peopl e tried by all means to  extinguish the flames. With big buckets they dragged water from the river to the village. Etore was among them.     The water spirits watched the goings - on of the people and then Vara saw him for the first time. He had severe  burn inju ries, but he kept running into the village with a full bucket, ignoring his pain. Many people died that  night and the village burned down completely.   From now on, Vara watched the brave Etore and fell in love with him. It was a foolish love, but love is fo olish at  times, and Vara did something that had not been ventured into before. She got out of her element and followed  her love. Etore was startled by the sight of her, for she was a figure of water without firm contours. She was  beautiful, but also scary.   Vara stayed with him for a while, helping wherever she could. But she soon realized  that her love would be forever unrequited, because Etore married a woman. Vara left Etore and wanted to go  back to the river, forgetting her grief and her sisters and brot hers. But the water spirits denied her this wish  and punished her for her stubbornness. She could never return home and was banished.     It took some time for Vara to go to Etore again. Her sadness startled the peasants and, with compassion, offered  to conti nue to take care of the well - being of the people on the river. Vara accepted his offer and since this day  she is here and fulfills this task. Etore became the first keeper of the River Lands and until today this task is  passed on to the first offspring fro m his line. "   Kheela looked at her son.   

Sadly, this Vara looked at the water spirit. "And she can never go back?"   "No, she can not do that. The love she once felt for Etore has turned into great grief. She is lonely, very lonely  and yet for centuries she h as supported the keeper of the river country and for that I am very grateful to her.  One day you will take on this task and have it as a faithful companion by your side. She will carry on the legacy  of Etore, the simple farmer. "   The water spirit came to them and gently brushed the boy's hand. A faint hint of summer dew formed where  she had touched him and she disappeared.     THE TWO ORDERS     Far to the north of the Hadrischen sea lay the island Hadria. An inhospitable island  surrounded  by rough seas, whose steep, dark cliffs projected into the sea. The forces  of the sea brought storms that icy gnawed at the rocks, snow that spread over the  land and winds whose strength tore everything away. Farther south were the Misty  Islands and Cliffw atch, a castle built on a single, large rock. Varatan, the sea king,  lived there.     Life in Hadria was arduous, winter unbearable and people often suffered from hunger. In some years, when the  weather was a bit milder, barley and wheat could be grown, but t oo often the cold season came early and rain  and frost destroyed the plants. These times could only be overcome by livestock, because the animals gave milk  and eggs, but often they had to be slaughtered in bad times.     On this island lived the wizards of th e Yra feasts. They were friars dedicated to making life more bearable for  the people of Hadria. They were scholars and passed on their knowledge for generations. But each of them  knew that the help they could give was enough only until winter came back and   took the people they had  worked for.     One day, the most inquisitive of them left the path of sorcery, which directs and intensifies the inner power of  every thing and living thing. They began to impose their will on things, transform them and create them  anew.  They alienated their true meaning and purpose. They discovered the dark magic.     Among them was Orweyn, the most powerful of all sorcerers. He was inspired by the idea of  freeing the country  from the winter and taming the powers of the sea. Arcturus , the Lord of the Storms, Kenvilar, the Treacherous  and Octohan, the Master of the Deep, should bow to his will.     He  was  gathering  like - minded  people  and  spending  many  years  exploring  dark  magic.  In  the  nights  that  Orweyn bowed over the writings, he devise d a plan.     Magic weapons should be forged that enable a person to rebel against the forces of the sea and defeat them. But  who would dare to do such a daring venture? Orweyn himself was eager to learn, but not a martial warrior.     But one day fate should brin g him this warrior. A large ship reached the coast of Hadria. It was the Tambur and  her captain was the proud King of the Sea Varatan. His coming triggered a tumult as he brought along wheat,  rye and other foods. Barrels of wine and goat cheese from Storm  Valley, and even apple nuts and mushrooms  from the distant Dragonland, later to become known as the land of Andor.     When Orweyn heard of his arrival, he believed in a happy coincidence.     This Sea King, whose name meant fire son, seemed the right person for   his plans. He invited him in and it soon  became clear how right Orweyn was. Varatan told of his trip across the Hadrian Sea, the dangers he had defied,  and how much he wished that winter would finally be over. After eating and drinking warm mead, Orweyn  b egan telling of his plan to defeat the forces of the sea and banish the winter forever. Varatan's eyes lit up as he  heard of the magic weapons Orweyn wanted to forge.     That night should be the fate of Hadria turn.     And so the friars of the blacksmith start ed their dark work. As they worked, gray mist wafted over the fire,  threatening mischief.     

They created Varlion the Flaming Sword, a heavy two - handed sword blazing flames on the blade that only  extinguished when pushed into the scabbard. Orweyn's hammer, w hich he held in his own pocket and which  strengthened his wearer more and more with each fight. And finally, Varatan's helmet designed to protect the  king from the forces of the sea.     After they were finished, a message was sent to the Sea King. He had ret urned to Klippenwacht and meanwhile  started a fleet with the construction and manned them with good sailors from Klippenwacht and the other fog  islands.     When he reached Hadria, Orweyn handed over the magic weapons and watched proudly, but with bated heart s,  as Varatan Hadria left.     For a long time, the magician remained uncertain about the whereabouts of the Sea King. As he did so, he  became more involved with Dark Magic and the more he understood Dark Magic, the more his doubts became.  He sensed that she was taking her toll.     After  many months, a terrible storm swept over Hadria. And in that thunderous storm, Varatan suddenly  appeared. His fleet was destroyed. He had lost them in the fight against the powers of the sea and to punish him  for his presumption, they also destroyed the gr eat castle Klippenwacht. Now they approached Hadria.     Charged, the Sea King called on the friars to strike back. Arkteron, Kenvilar and Oktohan were to be wiped out,  but Orweyn refused. He had finally fully understood what dark magic was doing. She always  demanded more  than she gave and that had to end.     Instead, he ordered the construction of the Iron Tower. There should be included the magic weapons and the  acquired dark knowledge about magic.     After  the  tower  had  been  completed,  Orweyn  asked  the  friars  to  follow  him  to  the  tower,  because  their  knowledge must be closed to protect the people of Hadria. Only then could the powers of the sea be soothed.     He ordered the youngest sorcerers to lock him and his brothers in the tower. Orweyn prevailed against the  pr otests of King Varatan and his friars. He killed some of them by hand to erase their knowledge from the  world. The fear of the powers of the sea had broken his mind. He talked confused and before he was the last to  enter the tower, he prophesied the end of   Hadriah if the wizards ever disagreed and summoned them together.  Then he went into the Iron Tower and the gate was closed behind him and all magical knowledge. Orweyn and  his brothers were never seen again.     But his victim had not missed its effect. The  storm subsided, the powers of the sea were reconciled and sank  back into the depths. Only the cold and the winter stayed and should not give way anymore.       The young and far less skilled wizards stayed behind and from then on called themselves the wizard s of the  Iron Tower.     The Sea King stayed in Hadria. He joined the remaining wizards of Hadria and learned what they could teach.  Apparently, Varatan gave up all royal dignity and became one of them, but he quarreled with Orweyn's decision  to surrender to  the powers of the sea, leaving Hadria and the sea to the Eternal Winter.     He moved to Nordgard, the capital of Hadrias. There, according to legend, he nagged other dissatisfied wizards  around him. It turned out that many of them had retained some magical k nowledge, but Orweyn's eyes had  escaped and not been locked in the Iron Tower.     Varatan found a wife in Hadria and she soon gave him a son named Varkmar, which meant as much as a sea of  flames.     He grew up with a desire for power and the knowledge hidden   in the Iron Tower.     In later years, after Varkmar had learned all that remained of magical knowledge, his father died. Nevertheless,  his thirst for knowledge remained and he founded a new Order of Wizards: The Wizards of Fire. Those wizards  

who did not wa nt to put up with the Eternal Winter, who over the years demanded more and more the opening  of the Iron Tower to liberate the magic.     In the long, cold years, the wizards of the tower and sorcerers of the fire continued to separate. Dark magic  stood betwee n them and Varkmar stirred their hatred.     But when he had reached the zenith of his power, he sensed that he would never have the power to take the  Iron Tower to liberate the magic. During this time, his wife gave birth to a son. On the night of his birth,   the  eternal fires shone brightly, but over the island of Hadria a huge storm raged. Full of pride Varkmar looked at  his powerful son, in whose eyes a magical fire burned at birth. He hoped his son would fulfill Varatan's legacy  and accomplish what he had  never done:     Unleash the magic and destroy and burn the hated wizards of the Iron Tower. And so he gave his son the name  Varkur: The Flame.     But its story is told in another legend ...     VARATAN'S CURSE     "Pah, sailor's yarn!" King Varatan always said when someone told  him about the three powers of the sea. He said this until the day he  came across the most dangerous of them: Kenvilar, the treacherous  ones.   Although the mighty Octohan would bring a ship wit h its tentacles  to burst and Arcteron dreaded storms, Kenvilar was the most fatal  of them. Their problem was coupled with cruel wisdom.     One day, as she lay in wait for the king's ship and dragged several  sailors into the depths, she noticed a Varatanian a t the helm of the  two - master. He stood tall and strong. The crew tried to master the  danger with harpoons and sea swords, but Kenvilar hardly noticed  them.     She caught the young helmsman's eye, looked into his future, saw his potential and the sleeping mali ce in him.  Kevilar sensed that she could do much more damage with a little patience. And so she retired.     The king celebrated his supposed victory over one of the three powers of the sea with everything that belonged  to it. The survivors were honored and t he dead were thought. Wine was drunk and lavishly fed. The festival was  remembered for a long time.   Years passed before the paths of the helmsman and Kenvilar crossed again. The name of the man was Callem.  He had meanwhile received command of his own ship  and sailed between Varatania or Werft home, as it was  later called, and Klippenwacht, the maritime stronghold of King Varatan.     On one of these trips, he left his route for no apparent reason and soon found himself in stormy waters again.  Kenvilar showed u p there and the former helmsman fell under his spell ...     The ship and its crew were soon lost and mourned with all imaginable honors. Callem, her captain, had been a  well - known naval warrior and his death meant a heavy loss to the king.     It was the time w hen Varatan began to ponder how to master the powers of the sea. A little later, his path  would lead him to the north, to Hadria in the land of sorcery, where he was to develop magical weapons with  Orweyn, the most powerful sorcerer.     But before all this h appened, rumors started about a black ship. It came out of nowhere and vanished in the  same way! Merchant ships were attacked and robbed of their goods. Here and there the black ship was spotted  and its crew ... it was the strangest thing, because on board   were not just simple sailors and apostate sea  warriors. Among them were sorcerers and wizards, druids and other powerful beings. Therefore, it was not  possible for a long time to get to the black cog, as the ship was now called everywhere.     

After his allege d death Callem had destroyed his ship, because Kenvilar had given him a much larger and  stronger as a gift. He killed most of his team with his own hands. It was a bloodbath. Roa, the huge bird of prey,  with claws, pointed and sharp like a sword and with h is red shimmering plumage, helped him. Only Pero, his  first Mart and Krumm, an old, bowed man whom they were supposed to bring to Varatania, remained alive.     The old crook claimed to be a sorcerer and brewed a potion to prove that he dipped the ship in thi ck fog. Callem  found it useful. In his cabin, the captain of the ship found a green - skinned girl with devious eyes. Another gift  Kenvilars, because it was Kentar, her daughter. The ship was to become her new home.   And so they set sail and with almost every   one of their raids the crew grew. During a raid near Stormtal,  Thogger, a Druid of the Tars joined. His potions gave all crewmembers great powers and the ability to breathe  underwater.     In another raid, you captured Ean Quella. A student from Hadria who w anted to complete her training as a  sorceress  while  traveling.  For  a  long  time  she  resisted  Callem's  influence.  Eventually  Kentar,  Kenvilar's  daughter, managed to poison her mind. And so she put her skills in the service of the captain.     Callem sought the  crown of the northern seas, and his power grew steadily. At some point the threat of the  Black Congue became so great that King Varatan rested his fight against the forces of the sea and set out in  search of the Black Cog.   Finding the hated ship and corner ing it required the king's entire naval fleet. At a tremendous speed, which  could not be attributed solely to the wind, the Black Cog evidently fled westward. Hoping to catch up with them,  King Varatan and his fleet pursued the ship, when suddenly, out of  nowhere, the coast of an unknown land  loomed before them. A mist island whose existence had been unknown to the king until then. This must have  been the secret hideout from where the Black Cog had started their raids. The gray sail of the cog was reefed  an d let boats into the water at lightning speed. The crew fled to the mist island. The king did not think long and  took up the chase. When they reached the island, the sea warriors stormed Varatans, killing anyone they could  get hold of.     Steep mountain ranges   towered before them, and when the king reached the first peak, his breath caught.  Behind the mountains lay a dark, sick forest. His smell of decay struck him from afar. He suddenly recognized  sinister lizard - like creatures crawling out of rocky outcroppin gs. They were Gors or maybe worse. This land  was a bad place and a deadly trap. A trap he was not allowed to touch. In his mind he baptized the island in the  name of Narkon, for that was how the Varatanians called a trap or an ambush, and he ordered his se a - warriors  retreat. Some did not hear his call and continued the persecution. Among those who fought most eagerly behind  the refugees was also his old Kamarad Ruuf. A good man. 'Be that as it may,' thought the king, 'I too can not help  him'.   There was more   at stake here than the lives of a few. And so King Varatan, ruler of the North Sea, spread his  arms and swore a curse upon the land north of the mountain. Let the creatures and apostates never leave this  island again and starve forever in suffering and mi sery. He cursed the land of Narkon and retired with his own.     Callem, however, who had hidden within earshot of the king, immediately sensed a change in mind and body.  Fear and anger flowed through him. Then he suddenly saw a ghostly figure of light, placi ng a gleaming hand on  his shoulder. All at once he forgot the sea and the ships and on all the memories that lay far away from this  island, the black shadow of forgetfulness lay down. Every thought of flight requires a perception of another  place, or at le ast the hope of the existence of a place other than the here. But all those who succumbed to the  curse were forever robbed of this idea.     More than a hundred years passed. Years in which the magic weapons in Hadria were forged and closed again,  because their power was too great and too dangerous. Years in which Varatan died and a young wizard named  Varkur, who came from Varatan's line, saw t he light of day to cause great evil. Years when a slave from  southern Krahd fled into the land of the dragon, defeated him and then founded the land called Andor. Years  when a small group of heroes became legendary and two of them stranded on the cursed is land of Narkon.     Chada and Thorn. Will you meet Callem and the cursed Black Cog crew? Will they succumb to Varatan's curse  and never leave the island?     

THE GIFT OF THE MAGICIAN     This story happened around the same time as the Heroes of Andor  denied the Battle   of Cavern. It is anticipated that this attack of the  creatures on the realm of the shield gnomes was no coincidence, but  the first step of a grand plan ...     Spoiler warning   for those who have not yet played "The Journey to  the North".     Prince  Undavahr  sta red  into  the  evening  sky. But one day the dwarves began to wrest new wonders from the fire. At first they began to forge beautiful  vessels and lamps, and later chains and rings as edging for the gems of the dee p. When Hallwort walked into the armory on that morning mentioned above and put on the finely crafted mai l  shirt, the gold breastplate, and put on the large square helmet, he noticed a sign in the corner.
